Tuzser Jewish Cemetery One

Jewish Cemetery · Tuzsér, Hungary

Not demolished. The first of Tuzsér's two Jewish cemeteries appears on an 1870 cadastral map; only one gravestone, dated 1906, remains legible today. Jews are first recorded in Tuzsér's 1747 census, numbering 37 by 1836; the community later shrank to 82 (of 1,060 residents) by 1880 and just 55 (of 2,019) by 1941. Tuzsér's Jews worked variously as retailers, draymen, smallholder farmers, and horse traders, joining the Orthodox community of Mándok in 1885. In mid-April 1944, following Passover, residents were gathered in the synagogue and transported to the Kisvárda Ghetto; their homes were sealed with red wax, and by late May they were deported to Auschwitz. Only about 10 returned after the war - some sheltered by Christian friends - and by 1949 just 3 Jews remained in Tuzsér.
